{{Short description|French particle physicist (1929–2020)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2019}}
'''André Jean Martin''' (20 September 1929 in [[Paris]] – 11 November 2020 in [[Geneva]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=André Martin (1929 – 2020)|url=https://home.cern/news/obituary/cern/andre-martin-1929-2020|access-date=2021-01-12|website=CERN|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hommages - Pour que son souvenir demeure: André MARTIN|url=http://hommages.ch/Defunt/131425/Andr%C3%A9_Martin|access-date=2020-11-20|website=hommages.ch}}</ref>) was a French particle [[physicist]] who worked at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] and [[CERN]].

== Biography ==
After studying at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] (class of 1949),<ref name="archicubes">{{cite web|url=https://www.archicubes.ens.fr/lannuaire#annuaire_chercher?identite=Andr%C3%A9+Martin.|title=L'annuaire {{pipe}} a-Ulm|website=archicubes.ens.fr|accessdate=2019-12-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150520151458/http://www.archicubes.ens.fr/lannuaire#annuaire_chercher?identite=Andr%C3%A9+Martin.|archive-date=20 May 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> he began his career as a CNRS researcher under the direction of [[Maurice Lévy (physicist)|Maurice Lévy]] at the physics laboratory of the École Normale. He joined CERN in 1959 as a fellow in the Theory Division and became a permanent [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] in 1964.{{citation needed|date=December 2019}}

In 1958 he helped found the Institut d'Études Scientifiques de [[Cargèse]] (Corsica).<ref>Luc Allemand et Vincent Moncorgé, Les jardins de la physique, CNRS éditions, 2017, <abbr>p.</abbr> 38</ref>

In 1959 he married Alice-Anne Schubert, known as Schu, who died in 2016, and had two sons, Philippe and Thierry.{{citation needed|date=December 2019}}

In 1994, he received the status of Physicist Emeritus, a status which has been renewed to this day. André Martin had scientific contacts all over the world: Europe, Asia, North America. He has made numerous visits to the United States, including two one-year visits to the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] at the invitation of [[J. Robert Oppenheimer|J.R. Oppenheimer]] and to [[New York University]], [[Stony Brook University|Stony Brook]], at the invitation of [[Yang Chen-Ning|C.N. Yang]].{{citation needed|date=December 2019}}

== Scientific work ==
The most interesting results of Maurice Lévy's thesis are the reconstruction of a separable interaction from a phase shift<ref>A. Martin et M.Gourdin., « Exact determination of a phenomenogical separable interaction », ''Nuovo Cimento'', 11 (1959), <abbr>p.</abbr> 670</ref> and an original demonstration of [[Levinson's theorem]].<ref>A. Martin, « On the validity of the Levinson Theorem for non local interactions », ''Nuovo Cimento'', 7, ( 1958), <abbr>p.</abbr> 607</ref> At CERN he first worked on the analytical properties of the amplitude of scattering by a potential: on the one hand a demonstration of the [[Mandelstam]] representation for a [[Yukawa potential|Yukawa]] potential,<ref>A.Martin, J. Bowcock. A Mandelstam, « Representation for potential scattering », ''Nuovo Cimento'', 14, ( 1959), <abbr>p.</abbr> 516</ref> on the other hand a new method for studying partial waves using the [[Laplace transform]].<ref>A.Martin, « Analyticity of partial waves obtained from the Schrödinger equation », ''Nuovo cimento'', 14, (1959), <abbr>p.</abbr> 516</ref>

After the proof, due to Froissart, that the total effective cross section cannot grow faster than the [[logarithm]] squared of the energy, using the Mandelstam representation,<ref>M.Froissart, « Asymptotic Behavior and Subtractions in the Mandelstam Representation », ''Phys. Rev'', 123, (1961), <abbr>p.</abbr> 1053</ref> he becomes interested in the amplitude of high-energy scattering. He demonstrates that Froissart's result for fixed-angle scattering can be improved.<ref>A.Martine, T.Kinoshita et J.J. Loeffel, « A new upper bound for fixed angle scattering amplitudes », ''Phys. Letters'', 10, (1963), <abbr>p.</abbr> 460</ref> Finally, in 1966, he succeeded in demonstrating the validity of the Froissart bound using local field theory, without postulating the Mandelstam representation.<ref>A.Martin, « Extension of the axiomatic analyticity domain of scattering amplitudes by unitarity: », ''Nuovo Cimento'', 42, (1966), <abbr>p.</abbr> 930</ref> In the meantime, in 1964, he obtains an absolute bound on the pion-pion scattering amplitude,<ref>An absolute bound on the pion pion scattering amplitude, Stanford Preprint ITP-1 (1964) non publié</ref> this bound was considerably improved later.<ref>B. Bonnier, C Lopez et G.Mennessier, « Improved absolute bounds on the π0π0 amplitude », ''Physics Letters B'', 60, (1), 22 December 1975, <abbr>p.</abbr> 63-66</ref>

He also proved the convergence of Padé's approximates for the levels of the anharmonic oscillator.<ref>A. Martin, J.J. Loeffel, B. Simon, and A Wightman, « Padé: Approximants and the anharmonic oscillator », ''Phys. Letters'', 30b, (1969), <abbr>p.</abbr> 656</ref> He treated the relativistic effects on the instability of [[boson]] stars.<ref>A.Martin, S.M. Roy, « Semi relativistic stability of systems with gravitationnal interactions », ''Phys Letters'', b233 (1989), <abbr>p.</abbr> 409</ref><ref>A.Martin, J.C.Raynal, S.M.Roy, J.Stubbe and V.Singh, « The Herbst Hamiltonian and the mass of boson stars », ''Phys. Letters'', b320 (1994), <abbr>p.</abbr> 105</ref>

In 1977, stimulated by experimental results on [[quarkonium]], formed from a heavy [[quark]] and [[antiquark]], he began to study the order of energy levels in potentials, but it was not until 1984 that the best criterion, the [[Laplacian]] sign of potential, was found.<ref>A.Martin, B.B, Aumgartner et H Grosse, « Order of enertgy levels in potential models », ''Nuclear Physics'', b254, (1985), <abbr>p.</abbr> 528</ref> At the same time, in 1981, he proposed a naïve model of potential to reproduce the levels of quarkonium, whose predictive power is extraordinary.<ref>A.Martin, « A simultaneous fit of bb, cc, ss, and cs spectra », ''Phys Letters'', 100b, (1981), <abbr>p.</abbr> 511B</ref> This model was also applied to [[baryon]]s formed from 3 quarks with great success by Jean Marc Richard.<ref>J.M.Richard, « Nonperturbative quark dynamics in baryon », ''Phys. Letters'', 100b, (1981), <abbr>p.</abbr> 515</ref> An overview of these results can be found in the book written with H.Grosse<ref>A.Martin et H, Grosse, Particle Physics and the Schrödinger equation, Cambridge University Press, 1997</ref> and a more recent unpublished review can be found in ArXives.<ref>Status of Heavy Quark Systems, ArXiv:0705.2353v1{ hep-.th} 15 May 2007, unpublished</ref>

He invented a geometrical method to study the stability of 3-body charged particle systems.<ref>A.Martin, J.M. Richard et T.T. Wu, « Stability of three unit-charge systems », ''Phys. Rev'', a43, (1992), <abbr>p.</abbr> 3697</ref><ref>A.Martin, A.Krikeb, J.M.Richard, et T.T. Wu, « On the stability domain of three arbitrary charges », ''Few body systems'', 29 (2000), <abbr>p.</abbr> 237</ref>

André Martin has also studied low-energy scattering in the case of two dimensions of space<ref>A.Martin, K Chadan, N.N Khuri et T.T.Wu, « Universality of low energy scattering in 2+1 dimensions », ''Phys REVD58'', (1998)</ref> as well as the counting of related states.<ref>A.Martin, T.T.Wu, « Bound states in 2 space dimensions in the non central case », ''Journ Math Phys'', 45, (2004), <abbr>p.</abbr> 923</ref>

Recent work (after 2008) includes a lower bound on the inelastic rms cross-section,<ref>A.Martin, S.M. Roy, « A lower bound on the inelastic cross-section for pion-pion scattering », ''Phys. Rev. D'', 96 ( 2017), <abbr>p.</abbr> 114014</ref> the sign of the real part of the forward scattering amplitud<ref>A. Martin, T.T.Wu, « Positivity of the real part of the forward scattering amplitude », ''Phys. Rev D'', 97 (2018), <abbr>p.</abbr> 014011</ref> and a lower bound on the wide-angle scattering amplitude.<ref>A.Martin, H.Epstein, « A rigorous lower on the scattering amplitude at large angle, ArXiv », ''soumis à Physical Review'', 2019 1903.00952 hep-th</ref>

== Books ==

*F. Cheung and A. Martin: Analyticity Properties and Bounds on Scattering Amplitudes, Gordon nd Breach 1970
*A.Martin: Scattering Theory: Unitarity, Analyticity and Crossing, Notes byR Schrader, Springer-Verlag 1969
*(en) Harald Grosse (de) and A. Martin, Particle Physics and the [[Schrödinger equation|Schrödinger Equation]], Cambridge University Press, 1998 ({{ISBN|0-521-44425-X}}, read online [archive]).

== Awards ==

*[[Doctor Honoris Causa|Doctor honoris Causa]] of the [[University of Lausanne]], 1972.
*Corresponding member of the French Academy of sciences, 1980–2007.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-M/andre-martin.html|title=Académie des sciences|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>
*Chevalier of the Légion d'Honneur, 1992
*Foreign Associate of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]
*Foreign Associate of the [[Indian Institute of Science|Tata Institute]] (Bombay)
*Gian-Carlo Wick Gold Medal, 2007<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cds.cern.ch/journal/CERNBulletin/2007/38/News%20Articles/1054839?ln=fr|title=Un physicien du CERN reçoit la Médaille Gian Carlo Wick|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>
*[[Pomeranchuk Prize]], Moscow 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1271705?ln=fr|title=Le prix Pomeranchuk 2010 décerné à André Martin|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>
